Guests can land at Tullamarine and be here before the drinks are poured.

Having the airport inside the council area removes the transfer problem that usually decides where interstate and overseas guests stay, and it changes what a weekend programme can look like.

Melbourne Airport sits at Tullamarine inside the City of Hume, and that matters more than it sounds. An interstate or overseas guest can clear the terminal and be at a Hume venue within twenty minutes, and the hotels around the airport give you an accommodation block with no transfer to organise. If a meaningful share of your guest list is flying in, comparing event planners in Hume starts with that advantage rather than with the venue.

The council area has a second character at its northern end. Sunbury is semi-rural, with bluestone heritage and vineyard country around Bulla and Diggers Rest, so estate and winery style events are realistic here without a long drive. Hume also has very large Turkish, Lebanese, Iraqi and Assyrian communities and a strong reception centre culture built around large formal weddings, while Craigieburn and Mickleham keep adding big new houses.

In and around Hume

What are you planning in Hume?

Six briefs cover most of the local work, and the distinguishing question on many of them is who is travelling. A guest list that arrives by plane runs to a different schedule from one that drives.

Start with

Weddings

Large formal receptions are the local norm, frequently several hundred guests with a set banquet and a ceremony beforehand. Where Hume differs is the arrivals. If family is flying in from interstate or overseas, the programme starts on the Thursday or the Friday rather than on the day of the wedding.

Parties and milestones

Engagements, significant birthdays and graduation parties fill the reception centres and function rooms through Broadmeadows, Roxburgh Park and Craigieburn, usually seated and catered. Newer houses at Mickleham and Greenvale take an at home event, and the yards there are big enough for a marquee.

Corporate events

Airport proximity gives Hume a genuine share of conferences and meetings booked precisely because delegates can fly in and out on the same day. The logistics and freight operations around Tullamarine add staff nights, awards and safety days, and those run to shift patterns rather than office hours.

Engagement parties

Commonly a full evening event with several hundred guests, booked months before the wedding and often the first time both extended families meet. If relatives are travelling from overseas for it, tie the date to their flights early, since visitor timing rather than venue availability usually decides the weekend.

Proposals

The vineyard country around Bulla and Diggers Rest and the open ground north of Sunbury give you rural settings twenty minutes from the suburbs. Check access and the light, and remember that ground which is firm in February can be soft and slow to drive on in July.

Private celebrations

Religious milestones, naming ceremonies, memorials and family gatherings are steady work here and usually catered sit down events. Where relatives arrive from overseas, the date is often set by a visa or a flight rather than by preference, which shortens the planning window considerably.

How much help do you want in Hume?

What decides the level of help here is often the guest list rather than the room. If people are flying in, someone has to manage arrivals, accommodation and a programme running across several days, and that is planning work rather than coordination.

Wedding coordination

A wedding coordinator takes a plan you have already built and runs the day itself, so nobody in the wedding party is directing traffic.

Choosing well

Finding the right planner in Hume

Ask a planner about arrivals, accommodation and the northern end of the council area. These four questions get at what is genuinely different about running an event in Hume.

No. 01

Ask how they manage an arriving guest list

If forty people are flying in across three days, someone has to know who lands when, where they are staying and how they reach each part of the programme. Ask whether the planner builds an arrivals schedule, whether they hold hotel blocks near the airport, and who guests contact when a flight is delayed on the Friday night.

No. 02

Ask what they have run at a reception centre

Large formal receptions here follow a set structure, with a ceremony, a staged banquet and a long evening. Ask for the biggest event a planner has run in the last two years, how many staff were on the floor, and where they placed the speeches. The answer tells you whether the run sheet will hold once the room is full.

No. 03

Ask about Sunbury specifically

The northern end behaves like country rather than suburb. Suppliers charge travel to reach Bulla, Diggers Rest and the properties beyond Sunbury, accommodation is thin, and a rural site may need generators, water and temporary bathrooms. Ask which venues up there a planner has actually worked at and what each site needed brought in.

No. 04

Check the flight noise if you are outdoors

Parts of Hume sit under approach and departure paths for Melbourne Airport, and an outdoor ceremony without amplification is where that shows. Ask whether the planner has run an event at your site, or visit it yourself at the same hour on the same day of the week. It is a five minute check that prevents a specific problem.

An airport inside the council area is the rarest logistical advantage on this list. Use it deliberately.

On the ground

An airport, a reception centre belt and open country

Three things define planning in Hume: guests who arrive by air, a strong tradition of large formal receptions, and a northern end that turns rural within about twenty minutes.

The airport removes the transfer problem

Having Melbourne Airport inside the council area changes what a weekend programme can look like. Guests flying in can be at a venue within twenty minutes of collecting bags, and the hotels clustered around Tullamarine give you a block of rooms with no coach between the beds and the event. That matters most for families arriving from overseas, who typically land days early and stay days after. Build an arrivals schedule rather than only a guest list, note who lands when, and decide in advance who meets a delayed flight at eleven at night.

Reception centres and how they run

Hume has very large Turkish, Lebanese, Iraqi and Assyrian communities and a well established reception centre culture built around large formal weddings. Those rooms are designed for the job, with staged service and their own supplier relationships, and they run to a known structure. What varies is what is included. Confirm in writing whether the venue provides styling, whether an outside caterer is possible, how many service staff sit in the quote, what time the room has to be cleared, and who takes the ceremony if it happens on site.

Twenty minutes north and it is country

Sunbury and the land around Bulla and Diggers Rest are semi-rural, with bluestone heritage buildings and vineyard country, which puts an estate style event within reach of the suburbs.

Questions

Planning an event in Hume

How much does an event planner cost in Hume?

Scope sets the fee rather than the suburb. Airtasker (updated February 2025) gives a national picture of event planning at $1,000 to $20,000, with hourly rates of $70 to $120 and around 10 to 15 per cent of total budget as a common alternative model. A large reception with interstate arrivals, a multi day programme and accommodation to manage sits at the upper end, so describe the whole weekend when you ask for a price.

Does having the airport nearby actually help?

Yes, and more than people expect. Melbourne Airport sits inside the City of Hume at Tullamarine, so guests flying in can reach a local venue within about twenty minutes, and the hotels around the airport work as an accommodation block with no transfer to organise. For a wedding with interstate or overseas family, that removes the coach problem and lets you hold a welcome event on the Friday without anyone driving.

Will aircraft noise affect an outdoor ceremony?

It can, depending on where you are and which runways are in use. Parts of Hume sit under approach and departure paths, and an outdoor ceremony without amplification is where it becomes obvious. The check is simple: stand at the site at the same hour and the same day of the week you intend to use it. If it is noticeable, either amplify the ceremony properly or move it inside.

Can we hold a wedding on rural land near Sunbury?

Yes, and the country around Bulla, Diggers Rest and north of Sunbury is close enough to the suburbs to make it practical. Treat it as a build. Power usually means a generator, water and temporary bathrooms have to be brought in, and a marquee needs firm ground, which winter does not always provide. Accommodation up there is limited, so check where guests will sleep before you commit to the site.

How far ahead should we book a large reception here?

Nine to fourteen months for a Saturday, and earlier if overseas family need time to arrange travel. The reception centres in this area are booked well ahead for spring and autumn, and the date frequently has to satisfy a religious calendar as well. If relatives are flying in, work backwards from their travel rather than forwards from the venue, since flights and visas are the least flexible part.

Do planners here manage accommodation for guests?

Some do and some do not, so ask before assuming. What is worth requesting specifically is a room block near the airport with a held rate, a list of who is staying where, and one contact for guests who need to change a booking. On a wedding with forty travelling guests, that single piece of administration is the difference between a plan and forty separate phone calls to you.
